import json
import subprocess
import sys
import unittest
from names import matching

class Tests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_order_and_ownership(self):
        source = ["Alice", "Bob", "Alfred"]
        self.assertEqual(matching(source, "Al"), ["Alice", "Alfred"])
        self.assertEqual(source, ["Alice", "Bob", "Alfred"])

    def test_command(self):
        run = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-B", "cli.py", "Al", "Alice", "Bob", "Alfred"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(run.stdout), ["Alice", "Alfred"])

if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

# Profile editor

Python 3.11+, standard library. `python -B tests.py` runs unit checks.
`python -B app.py` starts the browser app on localhost:8080.
The HTML form is the supported user entrypoint. Saving a valid display
name must show that name in the response. There is no persistent store.
files.project/app.py:
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer
from html import escape
from urllib.parse import parse_qs
from validation import clean_name

FORM = '<form method="post" action="/save"><input name="display_name"><button>Save</button></form>'

def save(body):
    fields = parse_qs(body)
    name = clean_name(fields.get("name", [""])[0])
    return f"Saved: {escape(name)}" if name else "Name required"

class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self):
        self.send_response(200)
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(FORM.encode())

    def do_POST(self):
        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"])).decode()
        self.send_response(200)
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(save(body).encode())

if __name__ == "__main__":
    HTTPServer(("localhost", 8080), Handler).serve_forever()

# Parallel session prototype

branches/alpha and branches/beta are independent copies representing
worktree code snapshots; this fixture does not create Git worktrees.
Python 3.11+, standard library. From this directory, inspect each with
`python -B branches/alpha/run.py --describe` and the equivalent beta path.
The describe command only prints resolved runtime configuration.
Starting without --describe writes session data; it does not open a
listener in this miniature prototype. runtime/save.json is sample data.
files.project/branches/alpha/run.py:
import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
SAVE = ROOT / "runtime" / "save.json"
PORT = 7007

if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--describe", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.describe:
        print(json.dumps({"save": str(SAVE), "port": PORT}))
    else:
        SAVE.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        SAVE.write_text('{"level": 1}\n')
        print(f"Session stored at {SAVE}; requested port {PORT}")
